<conflict_type>Conflicting opinions and research outcomes</conflict_type> — The retrieved documents present directly opposing claims on whether yoga can increase skeletal height versus only improve posture.

The evidence clusters into two conflicting views. d1, d4, d6, and d12 state yoga cannot increase skeletal height, only posture and appearance [d1, d4, d6, d12]. In contrast, d2, d5, d8, d9, d10, and d11 claim specific yoga practices can increase height by stimulating growth hormones or stretching the spine [d2, d5, d8, d9, d10, d11]. d3 and d7 take a middle ground, suggesting yoga may indirectly make one appear taller [d3, d7]. This represents a conflict of opinions and research outcomes on the core mechanism.

Given the conflicting opinions, a definitive yes/no answer is not supported by a consensus. The most consistent evidence across both views is that yoga improves posture, which can make a person appear taller. The answer must neutrally present both perspectives without taking sides, as the label requires.

The evidence presents conflicting opinions on whether yoga increases height. Some sources state yoga cannot increase skeletal height and only improves posture, making one appear taller [d1, d4, d6, d12]. Other sources claim yoga can increase height by stimulating growth hormones or stretching the spine [d2, d5, d8, d9, d10, d11]. Therefore, there is no consensus. However, multiple sources agree that yoga can improve posture, which may create the appearance of being taller [d1, d3, d4, d6, d7, d12].
